title: Power cut: what food to keep or throw out
version: MPI / New Zealand Food Safety fact sheet 'Food safety in the home after flooding' (Feb 2023, document 55615); MPI web page 'Food safety in natural disasters and emergencies' (Last reviewed 24.02.25); NEMA Civil Defence consistent messages 'Response: What to do in an emergency' and Get Ready 'No power' (no dates shown); Northland Regional Council 'Food safety - power cuts' (no date); Auckland Regional Public Health Service news 'Preventing foodborne illness when the power's out' (no date); Queenstown Lakes District Council poster 'How to keep food safe in a power cut' (Sep 2023, advice from Public Health Service - Southern); FSANZ 'Food safety in an emergency' (last updated 2 October 2025); all read 19 Nov 2026 NZ time
sourceNote: Every site blocks direct download here (curl refused by the proxy for mpi.govt.nz, getready.govt.nz, nrc.govt.nz, qldc.govt.nz, arphs.health.nz, foodstandards.gov.au and the Health NZ Hawke's Bay PDF mirror) and web search gave titles only, so every line was read by a fetch tool asked to quote short exact sentences (long ones in pieces, rejoined). Sections A (MPI web page), B (MPI fact sheet), C (NEMA consistent messages), E (Northland Regional Council, including the whole frozen-food table) and F (ARPHS) had every number and every 'do not / should not / only / except' line confirmed EXACT in a second read; D (Get Ready), G (QLDC poster) and H (FSANZ) were read once. One MPI sentence in A is missing its opening words (marked). Small slips (apostrophe or dash style) are possible. Eight labelled sections: A MPI emergencies page (food only), B MPI fact sheet (power failures, refreezing, disposing; flood, garden, hygiene, water and kai moana parts left out), C NEMA power-failure food lines, D Get Ready 'Fridge first', E Northland Regional Council (power cut text, frozen-food table and hygiene; flood paragraph left out), F ARPHS, G QLDC poster (box order approximate), H FSANZ (Australia-NZ joint agency). No US source was used. No PDF was in sources/. Oddities, gaps and contradictions: (1) fridge hold time differs: MPI, NEMA and the QLDC poster say an unopened fridge 'should hold refrigeration temperature for 4 hours', FSANZ says 'around four hours', but Northland Regional Council says 'at least 2 hours'; (2) freezer hold time differs: MPI/NEMA/QLDC say full 2-4 days, half full 1-2 days; Northland says half full 'up to 24 hours', full '48 hours'; FSANZ says a freezer 'shouldn't defrost for around 24 hours' with no full/half-full split; no source defines 'full' or 'half full' or covers a nearly empty freezer, chest vs upright, or opening the door; (3) temperatures: only Northland gives any, 5 degrees C (and 10 degrees C for some baked goods, fruit and vegetables in its table); MPI, NEMA and FSANZ give no temperature at all; no source mentions 4 degrees C or using a fridge/food thermometer; (4) time limit for thawed/warm food: Northland says above 5 degrees C for more than 2 hours; ARPHS says freezer food thawed and at room temperature for longer than two hours; Northland's table also has 'above 10°C for over 8 hours' for bread, muffins/cakes and vegetables; MPI gives no time limit, only 'if it has not started to look or smell bad'; (5) thawed food: MPI says thawed food can be kept or used if it does not look or smell bad and is kept cold, but Northland says 'Do not use frozen food that has thawed or refrigerated food that has warmed up' except butter/margarine, hard cheeses, raw eggs in shell, fruit and vegetables; ARPHS says you can still eat raw vegetables, cheese and bread and that fridge meat and fish 'may not be safe' 'after today' (no hour given); (6) Northland's table says ice cream and frozen yoghurt are thrown out even when still frozen with ice crystals, which conflicts with MPI's general 'still visibly frozen ... you can safely refreeze it'; its fruit row says refreeze even when thawed above 5 degrees C for over 2 hours unless mould, yeasty smell or sliminess develops; (7) no NZ source gives a food-by-food list for fridge (not freezer) foods beyond Northland's short exceptions list and ARPHS's raw vegetables, cheese, bread; nothing on leftovers, cooked rice, deli meats, sauces, baby formula/breast milk or medicines such as insulin; (8) MPI's freezer refreeze rule needs packaging 'isn't damaged or open', ARPHS says 'packaging is intact'; Northland's table does not mention packaging; (9) no source says how to tell how long the power was off or how warm the food got (no clock, thermometer or ice-cube tips), nor what to do if you were away; (10) the MPI web page and FSANZ tell you to check smell, look, colour and texture, and FSANZ says 'Don't taste it'; (11) eating order: MPI and NEMA say fridge first, then freezer, then pantry/cupboard; MPI's emergencies page examples are only bread and meat, the fact sheet adds salads and dairy; (12) FSANZ alone suggests eskies with ice bricks or gel packs, and no NZ source mentions chilly bins, ice or moving food elsewhere; (13) Northland's page names no source organisation; its table looks adapted from overseas (10 degrees C / 8 hours) but this is not stated; (14) the MPI fact sheet was written for floods (Cyclone Gabrielle, Feb 2023), not power cuts alone; MPI has no stand-alone power-cut page that could be found; (15) the MPI fact sheet line 'and cause of food poisoning' is a typo in the source, kept as printed.
status: Reviewer: 1 instruction missed (check the label) and 14 findings, incl. a dead end while the power is still off; all fixed. 122 of 122 quotes exact (web copy).
